concept: One meeting room, one comment rebuilt in front of us. A friendly, vague line after an overrun gets a nod and changes nothing; the clock overruns again. A label makes it worse; what the clock showed is the usable part. The same bubble becomes a message card that grows line by line (what you saw, its impact, an agreed next step) while the colleague's face moves from easy to attentive. The viewer checks it on a handover note missing a deadline, sees the talk done soon and two-way in a quiet corner, sees praise made specific at their own desk, gets a blank card to fill, and the room returns a week on with the clock on the end mark.

stations.note: Asha (the giver) screen left facing right, Ben (the colleague who runs the meeting) screen right facing left (flip), peep busts behind the table; wall clock upper right; the message card in the wall centre between them.
An everyday desk with nobody at it: monitor, sticky notes, mug, plant. b06, b14, b15.
A desk top: the handover note left, three equal option cards in one column right, the question above. b11, b12.
Two soft chairs by a window, afternoon light; Asha left, Ben right, same sides and bust size as the room. b13.

story.metaphor: None: a literal workplace moment, rebuilt in place.
story.setting: A small meeting room after a weekly meeting that overran; a quiet corner the same afternoon; the viewer's own desk.
story.arc: A friendly vague line and a nod change nothing; a label would make it worse; the same line rebuilt as what was seen, its impact and an agreed next step; checked on a handover note; said soon and two-way; praise made specific; the next meeting ends on time.

devices.what: Asha's one speech bubble: the vague line (b01), emptied (b04), turned into a paper card that grows line 1 what you saw (b07), line 2 impact (b08), part tags and SBI once (b09), line 3 next step with an agreed tick (b10), edited small in the corner (b13), and as the viewer's blank four-slot card (b15).
The same meeting room two-shot, Asha left, Ben right, same looks and sides, faces carrying the reaction.
The room's wall clock with a small end-time mark: before the mark (b01), the hand past it (b02), the twenty-minute overrun arc shaded (b05, b07), the hand on the mark (b16).
The viewer's desk: a Good job sticky with an empty space where the action would be (b06); a Great job bubble beside a specific note tied to the timed agenda (b14); a blank four-slot card (b15).
The one join material: a paper page turn into the check (b11), into the quiet corner (b13), and at the week skip into the payoff (b16).

parts.what: The meeting room set: surface2 wall, field2 table front one value step from the wall, table top edge across the frame at about y 900 so peep busts placed before it are hidden below it; room for Asha's bust at x about 380 and Ben's at x about 1540 (size about 560, eyes in one band); the wall clock's place upper right; the card's space in the wall centre (about 820 x 420); space for two muted extras behind the table. Exports the anchors (asha, ben, clock, card, agenda_pin, extras). No people; no accent in the set.

A round wall clock, ink outline, surface face, with a small end-time tick on its rim. States: on_time (minute hand just before the mark), over (the minute hand sweeps past the mark on a cue), overrun_arc (the twenty minutes past the mark shaded as an arc; the accent only when named), at_end (the hand settles on the mark). No digits needed.

Asha's paper speech bubble that becomes a card, tail toward Asha (screen left), Nunito ink text. States: vague (one line: Maybe tighten it up?), empty (the bubble emptied to a dashed hollow: nothing to act on), card (the bubble reshapes into a card with three dashed empty slots), line1 (Tuesday's meeting ran twenty minutes over.), line2 (Two people missed their next call.), tags (small tags Situation, Behaviour on line 1 and Impact on line 2, and the small heading Situation, Behaviour, Impact (SBI)), slot3_open (the third slot pulses open), line3 (Could we try a timed agenda?), agreed (a small pos tick on line 3), small (the whole card scaled to about 520 wide for the corner, line 3 able to be struck and rewritten), blank_four (an empty card with four slots labelled Behaviour, Impact, Next step, Ask, each able to light in turn). One accent at a time: the line or slot being spoken; the others ink on surface.

A stick-on paper tag with the words You're disorganised in Patrick Hand 400. States: in_hand (near Asha), stuck (flies and sticks on Ben's chest), crossed (a neg cross lands on it), peeling (it peels and falls away).

A paper agenda sheet with three rows, each with a small drawn time box beside it that fills in turn (bars of length, no digits), titled Agenda. States: blank, filling (the time boxes fill row by row), pinned (the sheet small, pinned on the room wall beside the clock), thumb (a small drawing of it for a note).

An everyday desk with nobody at it: monitor (ink body, surface2 screen), a mug, a plant, an empty chair. States: thumbs_note (a sticky note reading Good job with a thumbs-up and a dashed empty space under it where the action would be), great_bubble (a plain speech bubble Great job, its inside empty of any action), specific_note (a second note beside it, heading What worked, so keep it, with the timed agenda thumb drawn in its space, joined to it by a line), card_space (room in the desk centre for the blank card). The note text is a parameter.

A desk top with a paper handover note left (rows Client and Open tasks, and a dashed gap where the client deadline row should be) and three equal option cards in ONE even column right: A You're not very detail-minded. B The handover could have been better. C Your note skipped the deadline; it slipped. List it next time? The question line above: Which line changes what happens next? A pause ring. States: note (the note lands, the gap shows), options (the cards arrive as peers, tight stagger), pause (the ring drains over the silent pause), c_right (a pos tick on C, its three parts underline in turn), b_hollow (B dims, three empty outline slots beside it), a_wrong (a neg cross on A), labels (one short label under each card: C: behaviour, impact, next step; B: polite, nothing to act on; A: about the person).

A quiet corner set: two soft chairs angled toward each other by a window with afternoon light, a small side table where the small message card lies; room for Asha's bust left and Ben's right, same sides and size as in the room; a small paper sign space for Soon, in private. No people; no accent in the set.

kit.notes: People are never in the kit: Asha and Ben are kit.peep busts placed by each scene with literal story.cast looks (Asha: woman, skin 2, cloth, screen left; Ben: man, skin 1, cloth2, flip true, screen right). Extras through ctx.crowd only, muted, behind the cast. Clothes never accent, accent2, pos or neg. The peep neutral face has closed eyes: never hold it on a listener past 4 s. Furniture never uses the accent.

scenes.subject: About the person versus what you saw

design.treatment: Two takes on the same meeting. A tag You're disorganised flies from Asha and sticks on Ben's chest; he bristles (surprised); a label About the person sits under it and a neg cross lands; the tag peels away. design.why_motion: the same moment named two ways, and the two reactions differ
